initial.name: bash
initial.description:
Run commands in a bash shell
* When invoking this tool, the contents of the "command" parameter does NOT need to be XML-escaped.
* You don't have access to the internet via this tool.
* You do have access to a mirror of common linux and python packages via apt and pip.
* State is persistent across command calls and discussions with the user.
* To inspect a particular line range of a file, e.g. lines 10-25, try 'sed -n 10,25p /path/to/the/file'.
* Please avoid commands that may produce a very large amount of output.
* Please run long lived commands in the background, e.g. 'sleep 10 &' or start a server in the background.

command.description: The bash command to run. Relative path is preferred in the command.

initial.name: doctor
initial.description: Read-only environment self-check of this Hydra installation: home, workspace folders, sandbox, native addon, git, mounted plugins, tool-calling compat rows, and credential references (never key values). Set probe to also send one tiny model request to the default route and report its latency or failure class.

probe.description: Also probe the default model route with one tiny request.

initial.name: journal
initial.description: The research journal of this workspace: the durable memory of a research goal across sessions. `breakthrough` records a confirmed step toward the objective; `hypothesis` adds one (text) or sets its status (id + status); `experiment` records what was tried and the result; `dead_end` records what must not be retried and why; `next` replaces the next steps; `read` returns the journal. Entries are written to the journal file at once and recalled into every later request, so record findings the moment they happen. `slug` defaults to the research this session runs.

slug.description: Journal slug; defaults to the active research of this session.

id.description: hypothesis: the hypothesis id to update.

status.description: hypothesis: the new status when `id` is given.

steps.description: next: the next steps in order.

initial.name: knowledge_add
initial.description: Index a folder of documents the user named, so this workspace can search it with the knowledge tools. Call it only when the user asks you to use, read, or learn from a folder of documents; the user approves the folder first and is asked separately before its files are summarized.

path.description: The folder the user named: absolute, relative to the workspace, or starting with ~.

name.description: A short collection name of letters, digits, - and _; the folder's name when omitted.

initial.name: memory
initial.description: Long-term memory across sessions. `remember` stores a durable fact, shortcut, or preference, or a lesson (a root cause found, an approach that failed and why, a corrected assumption) the user would want later work to know; `search` finds stored entries; `forget` deletes one by id. Entries related to the current work appear in <retrieved_memory>; use one only when its situation matches. Write each entry so it names its situation (the file, command, or component). Never remember plans or progress reports.

text.description: remember: the knowledge to store, one or two sentences.

query.description: search: words matched against entry text and tags, best match first; omit to list everything.

initial.name: run_experiment
initial.description: Run one research experiment as a shell command in the workspace and record it in the research journal: the command, exit code, metrics read from the output with your regular expressions, deltas against the previous run with the same `title`, and an output excerpt. Use it instead of `bash` for experiments so results are never lost. Requires an active research goal in this session (start one with /research).

title.description: Short stable name of the experiment; repeating a title yields per-metric deltas.

command.description: The shell command to run in the workspace directory.

hypothesisId.description: The journal hypothesis this experiment tests.

timeoutMs.description: Time budget in milliseconds; capped by the deployment maximum.

metrics.description: Metrics to read from stdout and stderr; the first capture group (else the whole match) must be a number.

initial.name: str_replace_editor
initial.description:
Custom editing tool for viewing, creating and editing files
* State is persistent across command calls and discussions with the user
* If `path` is a file, `view` displays the result of applying `cat -n`. If `path` is a directory, `view` lists non-hidden files and directories up to 2 levels deep
* The `create` command cannot be used if the specified `path` already exists as a file
* If a `command` generates a long output, it will be truncated and marked with `<response clipped>`
* A null placeholder for a parameter unused by the selected command is treated as omitted. Required parameters still need values; omit `str_replace.new_str` rather than setting it to null when deleting a match

Notes for using the `str_replace` command:
* The `old_str` parameter should match EXACTLY one or more consecutive lines from the original file. Be mindful of whitespaces!
* If the `old_str` parameter is not unique in the file, the replacement will not be performed. Make sure to include enough context in `old_str` to make it unique
* The `new_str` parameter should contain the edited lines that should replace the `old_str`

command.description: The commands to run. Allowed options are: `view`, `create`, `str_replace`, `insert`.

path.description: Absolute path to file or directory, e.g. `/repo/file.py` or `/repo`.

file_text.description: Required string parameter of `create` command, with the content of the file to be created. A null placeholder is treated as omitted by commands that do not use this parameter.

insert_line.description: Required integer parameter of `insert` command. The `new_str` will be inserted AFTER the line `insert_line` of `path`. A null placeholder is treated as omitted by commands that do not use this parameter.

new_str.description: Optional string parameter of `str_replace` command containing the new string (if omitted, no string will be added). Required string parameter of `insert` command containing the string to insert. A null placeholder is accepted only by commands that do not use this parameter.

old_str.description: Required string parameter of `str_replace` command containing the string in `path` to replace. A null placeholder is treated as omitted by commands that do not use this parameter.

view_range.description: Optional parameter of `view` command when `path` points to a file. If omitted or null, the full file is shown. If provided, the file will be shown in the indicated line number range, e.g. [11, 12] will show lines 11 and 12. Indexing at 1 to start. Setting `[start_line, -1]` shows all lines from `start_line` to the end of the file.

initial.name: usage
initial.description: Read-only token usage across every recorded session: overall totals, a table by provider and model, and a per-day series. Counts what providers reported for assistant messages, bucketed by the local day each message happened. Use since and until to look at one stretch of days.

since.description: Inclusive first local day as YYYY-MM-DD. Omit for all recorded history.

until.description: Inclusive last local day as YYYY-MM-DD. Omit to run to the most recent day.
